label: Easy Opener
source: The Ivy League official membership: https://ivyleague.com/
valueLogic: Harvard, Yale and Princeton are produced instantly. Columbia and Cornell follow. Brown and Penn sit in the middle, Penn partly because people confuse it with Penn State. Dartmouth is the tail - it is reliably the last of the eight anyone names.
note: Penn State and the other prestigious non-Ivies are non-busting distractors: the Penn/Penn State confusion is extremely common and the note explains it.

answers.name: Harvard University
answers.fact: Founded 1636, the oldest university in the country and the oldest of the eight.

answers.name: Yale University
answers.fact: Founded 1701, and the third-oldest university in the country.

answers.name: Princeton University
answers.fact: Founded 1746, and the only one of the eight with no medical or law school.

answers.name: Columbia University
answers.fact: Founded 1754 as King's College, and renamed after the Revolution.

answers.name: Cornell University
answers.fact: Founded 1865, by far the youngest of the eight, and partly a public land-grant school.

answers.name: Brown University
answers.fact: Founded 1764, and the first to accept students of all religious affiliations.

answers.name: University of Pennsylvania
answers.fact: Founded 1740 and shaped by Benjamin Franklin. Not Penn State, which is a different school entirely.

answers.name: Dartmouth College
answers.fact: Founded 1769, the smallest of the eight, and the only one still called a college.

distractors.name: Penn State
distractors.note: Pennsylvania State University - a different school, and not in the Ivy League.

distractors.name: Stanford
distractors.note: Prestigious, but not an Ivy. The Ivy League is an athletic conference in the northeast.

distractors.name: MIT
distractors.note: Not an Ivy, and in a different athletic conference.

distractors.name: Duke
distractors.note: Not an Ivy, despite the 'Southern Ivy' nickname.
